stem.text: A particle moves along the curve \( x y = 8 \) so that its coordinates \( x \) and \( y \) are differentiable functions of time \( t \). At the instant the particle is at the point \( (2, 4) \), the \( x \)-coordinate of the particle is decreasing at a rate of 3 units per second. Find \( \frac{dy}{dt} \), in units per second, at that instant.

worked_solution.text: Differentiate both sides of \( x y = 8 \) with respect to \( t \), using the product rule on the term that contains both variables: \( \left(y\right)\frac{dx}{dt} + \left(x\right)\frac{dy}{dt} = 0 \).
At \( (2, 4) \) the coefficient of \( \frac{dx}{dt} \) is \( 4 \) and the coefficient of \( \frac{dy}{dt} \) is \( 2 \). Substitute \( \frac{dx}{dt} = -3 \): \( (4)(-3) + (2)\frac{dy}{dt} = 0 \).
